topic: Higher Order Derivatives: Unveiling Rates of Change

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative
lecture_lines: First derivative represents instantaneous rate of change.
Slope of the tangent line indicates speed.
Position change over time defines velocity.
animations: Fade in title: 'Prerequisite Review: The First Derivative' (Color: #FFFFFF)
Draw tangent line segment with slope visualization (Color: #FFFF00)
Animate tangent line slope changing along path (Color: #FF00FF)

sections.title: Defining Higher Order Derivatives
lecture_lines: Second derivative is the derivative of the derivative.
Positive second derivative means concave up.
Negative second derivative means concave down.
It tracks how velocity changes over time.
animations: Fade in title: 'Defining Higher Order Derivatives' (Color: #FFFFFF)
Draw f(x) curve and tangent line (Color: #FFFFFF)

sections.title: Visualizing Physical Meaning
lecture_lines: Position graph shows location over time.
Velocity graph shows slope of position.
Acceleration graph shows slope of velocity.
animations: Show Position, Velocity, Acceleration stacked graphs (Colors: #FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF)
Animate moving object on Position-Time graph (Color: #FFFFFF)
Display velocity slope changing on graph (Color: #FFFF00)

sections.title: Calculation and Notation
lecture_lines: Leibniz notation uses d squared y dx squared.
Lagrange notation uses f double prime of x.
Power rule applies recursively to find derivatives.
animations: Animate step-by-step recursive power rule application (Color: #FFCC00)

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
lecture_lines: Third derivative is known as jerk.
Jerk impacts motion control and engineering.
Minimizing jerk ensures smooth robotic movement.
animations: Fade in title: 'Summary and Real-world Application' (Color: #FFFFFF)
